name: Unnamed healthcare-administration placement through a staffing chain

attribution.legal_posture: Official federal indictment; employment and device delivery remain allegations, and patient-data access is absent from the allegations.

caveats: Behavioral signals require corroboration and human review; staffing, badge, device, download, location, and sector signals become DPRK attribution only with supporting evidence.
Official federal indictment; employment and device delivery remain allegations, while patient-data access falls outside its allegations.

statements: The indictment alleges a successful contractor placement at an unnamed Missouri healthcare-administration company through a staffing chain. The end-client laptop was delivered to the domestic laptop-farm address; the filing does not allege patient-data access or compromise.
defensive_controls: Healthcare firms should independently re-proof remote contractors supplied by staffing firms before device shipment.
Correlate shipping address, tax/home address, device geolocation and identity-verification evidence across the staffing chain.
Do not infer access to patient data: the filing alleges employment and device delivery, not PHI access or compromise.
